notes: The numbers that belong to no single card: setup quantities, the standing economy rates, and the end-game trigger. Anything PRINTED on a card lives in cards.json instead, and anything printed on the island lives in island.json.

visitPayout is the machine-readable form of the payout printed on the Notice Board and on its upgraded face. The card text is the source; this is what the engine and the simulator read, so the two must not drift. The card is: base face VISIT, gain GBP 1 or take the action; upgraded face VISIT, gain GBP 2, or gain GBP 1 AND take the action. The owner is paid nothing on either face - visitWage stays 0 and the owner's return is the freight.

upgradedAction IS THE CARD (Dean, 2026-08-13). The upgraded face used to sweeten only the coin branch, and a probe measured what that actually bought: coin-branch take-up rose 1.36x at an upgraded board while the same host's action branch FELL to 0.87x, so most of the pull was a visitor swapping doors on one farm rather than choosing that farm over a neighbour's. Total traffic to an upgraded farm moved 1.08x raw, and 1.29x once the flat control arm (upgraded face, no payout advantage, which reads 0.84 because upgraded boards mostly exist late in the game) takes the time confound out. Paying both branches the same GBP 1 removes the reason to switch door and aims the money where the traffic is: per offer a visitor takes the action 25% of the time against the coin's 8%. Setting it to 0 restores the old face and is the paired control. NOTE the standing finding it has to live with - every coin minted into the visit loop also subsidises the bonus slot's SOLITAIRE option, because a visit is bought with a card and your own Service is bought with a coin. At 0.14 Notice Board flips per seat-game that drag is small, but it is why the owner is paid nothing.

twoCard was Special Orders' second line, "2 cards, take GBP 3". Change 6 retired Special Orders and the 2026-08-13 face replaces it, so nothing prints the line any more: it is NULL and visitOptions stops offering the mode. The engine keeps the code path so switching it back on is a data edit; delete it in its own commit if it is still null when the next rulebook ships.

coinPityDivisor turns leftover coins into VP at game end: floor(coins / divisor). It is now NULL - coins are worth no victory points at all. Settled by Dean on ticket 37 (2026-08-02), which measured the rule's real cost: 65% of every coin minted was never spent on anything, so at the printed divisor of 5 a typical end-game pile of GBP 37 was quietly worth 7 VP - close to a Level 2 delivery - for hoarding. That made the free visit a risk-free VP drip and left GROW competing against it for the same scarce card. Coins are spend-only, as the design has always said; they survive in scoring only as the first tie-break.

turn.buyCost is the card BUY (Dean, 2026-08-03): once a turn, as a free action, pay the bank and take the top card of a deck that is NOT your own suit. It is the answer to the Feld-lens finding that the game mints coins and is throttled by cards with no exchange between them - a coin now converts into the throttled resource, so coins are never dead. Blind, and deliberately not a Draw: no reveal, no keep, no draw modifier, so the Orchard Farmstead and the Draw Worker keep the draw lane. Null switches the rule off, which is the paired control in overlays/no-card-buy.overlay.json.

turn.marketCost is BUY AT MARKET as the parent design adopted it (docs/Market Bonus Action 2026-08-03.md): a third bonus-slot option beside the coin visit and the worker visit. Pay the bank, take the top card of ANY one deck in play - own suit included - straight into the BARN, revealed as it goes. It consumes the bonus slot, because competing with the visit is the entire point; it is not a visit (no Helping Hand, no afterVisit, no wage) and not a Draw (no reveal-and-keep, no draw modifier). Own suit is legal here and illegal at the buy, both deliberately: the barn destination makes own-suit harmless colour for delivery, the hand destination made it a second Draw. Null deletes the rule. Ticket 56 holds this and buyCost side by side so the paired arms can decide which coin sink is the game's - they are two different rules, not two prices for one.
startingBarnCards is the single card each player starts with in their barn. startingHand is drawn from their own suit deck, which is why an owned deck holds 12 cards after setup.

endGame.trigger is deliveryCount (owner, 2026-08-09, with the flat island): the game ends when any ONE seat completes its deliveriesToTrigger-th island delivery, after which every other player takes furtherTurnsEach more turns. It replaces levelThreeDelivery, which cannot survive an island with no levels. Two properties carried over deliberately. It is still ONE observable trigger read off public state - now a receipt count in front of a player rather than a token on the top row - and it is still a thing a player does rather than a deck running out. Balloon moves are Deliver actions but not island deliveries, so they do not count toward it. deliveriesToTrigger is FLAT at every seat count, which means the trigger fires at half the 2-seat island, a third of the 3-seat one and a quarter of the 4-seat one; that asymmetry is known and taken, and 2p is where to watch it.

upgradeCostCoins now prices ALL THREE starters. The Farmstead's free flip at three own-crop buildings was retired by Dean on 2026-08-12: it is bought for GBP 2 like the Barn and the Notice Board, so farmsteadFlipAtOwnColourBuilds is gone and the upgrade grammar is one line instead of two. What went with it: the game's only binary achievement, the second job the paid Barn/Notice Board flip used to do (its crop icon could complete the milestone), and the guarantee that every seat eventually gets its upgraded suit power. What arrived: a third competing GBP 2 sink, which is what the 2026-07-14 coin drought and the v14 coin flood both asked for. Untested at the table and untested in the simulator.

economy.giftDiscardCoins is the coin on the UPGRADED Orchard Farmstead's rebuilt power (docs/orchard-suit-rebuild-v5.md): "give the discarded card to a neighbour AND take GBP 1 from the bank". Its own knob because the rebuild's own risk list names it as the number most likely to be wrong - roughly GBP 8-10 a game where seats currently end with GBP 1 - and because it is the one part of a data-and-handler rebuild an overlay CAN express cleanly. 0 leaves the gift free, which is overlays/orchard-farmstead-coin.overlay.json. The base face never pays whatever this says; the coin is the whole of what the upgrade buys.
unresolved: W21 The Bread Hall prints "Game end: 1 VP for every GBP 2" and declares replacesCoinPity. With the pity now null there is nothing left to replace, so the card is no longer a better rate than everyone else's - it is the ONLY rate. Ticket 37 flagged it; the card's own value is a separate open question.

The Notice Board threshold is printed 5, with a proposed dial to 4 at two seats that has never been adopted. Not modelled: the printed threshold in cards.json is the only threshold. If the dial is adopted it becomes a seats-indexed override here.
